Invariant from the R0.4.5 review:

R0.4.6 freshness / anti-rollback model — written before the mechanism

Invariant from the R0.4.5 review:

An old valid lifecycle prefix must never reactivate possession that a newer finalized history has fenced. Recovery requires freshness, not merely internally valid history.

The hole

<!-- historical --> Before R0.4.6, recovery and (the since-removed) reopen proved possession against whatever event slice the caller supplied. A stale custody for A@0 fails against the current history, but succeeds against the old prefix [Attached(A,0)]. Same for reopen: a warden that never reopened plus an old closed prefix materializes a vacancy at a generation that is currently occupied via an orderly succession. Both are rollbacks: making an old truth current again. <!-- /historical -->

Closure: a linear, non-rollbackable current token

(Introduced in R0.4.6 as a "head" advanced in a separate step; since R0.4.7 the same linear value is the LifecycleAdmission and is advanced only by the transitions themselves — see docs/admission-model.md. The freshness property is unchanged.)

LocusRoot::begin() ─────────────► Vacant(0) + FinalityWarden + LifecycleAdmission(gen 0, vacant)
Vacant/Attachment/Warden + Admission ──transition──► ... + Admission'   [CONSUMES the admission]
CarrierCustody + &LifecycleAdmission ──recover──► LocusAttachment

  • LifecycleAdmission is born once per lineage at begin, has private

fields and no public constructor, is move-only, and advances only by being consumed by a transition. An older admission therefore cannot coexist with the current one as recovery authority: it was consumed to produce the current one.

  • Possession-granting operations no longer accept an event slice at all.

Passing &[LifecycleEvent] where a head is required is a compile error. "Caller must supply the latest log" is thereby encoded, not documented.

  • replay_lifecycle / audit_replay remain public and descriptive over

slices: knowledge of any prefix is still available; possession from a prefix is not.

What stays outside the claim (unchanged honest boundary)

  • A trusted root can fork lineages via repeated create_locus, each with

its own head; a fork can be fed the honest prefix and would recover the stale custody. Locus-birth uniqueness is the future World-level invariant; cross-lineage rollback resistance is not claimed.

  • Durable crash recovery and cross-process/disk copies remain unclaimed;

a persisted head is bytes and copies freely — the same future incarnation/CAS/fencing primitive applies to heads as to custody.

  • No distributed consensus, leases, or network protocol in this round.

Falsifiers this model must survive

  1. The review's 7-step scenario: stale A custody fails against the

current head; there is no API path to present the old prefix.

  1. At an occupied generation, finality of the wrong carrier/generation

fails and no second vacancy can be minted; no slice path exists.

  1. A consumed admission cannot be reused (compile gate); a failed

transition hands the admission back.

  1. LifecycleAdmission cannot be fabricated (private fields); recovery

rejects event slices (type error).

  1. All prior falsifiers remain green under the head-based API.
